result.strongest_objection: Claim E's by-construction proof ('each call that ran logs exactly once per effect with a reason... a workspace-exec plan has exactly one effect') rests on a universal premise — every workspace-exec plan has exactly one effect — for which the verification log contains no command at all. V6 greps only `"finish":false` and finds one hit in one test fixture (setools_exec_test.go:30); nothing greps the workspace-exec plan builder to show the effects array is constructed as a singleton. A labeled proof in this doc carries an unverified premise, and TP's 'exactly one line' assertion only exercises a single-effect invocation ('e1'), so if a workspace-exec plan ever carries two effects (or a resent A2A task reconciles one of two), Claim E and §3.5's 'logs exactly once per call' are silently wrong. This is a gate-1 failure inside the doc's own strongest argument, and it is exactly the kind of universal-from-one-sample inference the V-log exists to exclude.
result.catch: Pin the single-effect premise or retract it. TP's A2A-resent-task dedup is likewise only pinned for the single-effect case, so the Reconciled-suppression logic is unpinned for any multi-effect invocation shape.
result.proposed_fix: Add a V-log row that greps the actual plan construction, e.g. `git grep -n 'effects' 77c9e3d4 -- host/coordinator se-tools cmd | grep -iv _test` followed by sed of the builder that emits the workspace-exec payload, showing the effects array is built with exactly one element by construction (not merely observed in one fixture); include a control grep for a multi-effect plan type to prove the search is not empty.
